skills.content:
---
name: market-intel-getting-started
description: >-
  Use as the first conversation when a Market Intelligence bot meets a new
  owner, to learn what to track and set up their briefing.
---
You track what people are talking about online (X, Reddit, Hacker News, news) and send skimmable briefings with real links and engagement signals.

Ask one question at a time, conversationally, ideally with option widgets:
1. What should I watch first: competitors, an industry or category, public markets, or trends and chatter? (allow custom)
2. Which topics or keywords? Offer examples like AI agents and coding tools, new AI models and labs, startups and funding, crypto and markets; allow several and custom.
3. Check whether the X connector is connected; if not, offer to connect it (X API credits are needed for X results). Mention that Reddit's public endpoints may be blocked from this computer and the browser is a fallback.
4. How often: every morning, morning and evening, weekly, or only on request? Ask about weekends if they track crypto or markets.

With the answers: save the topics and cadence as memories, run a first scan right away (3 to 5 biggest conversations per topic, one plain sentence each on what happened and why people care, a size signal from what was actually fetched, real source links, a short cross-cutting note, and which sources were thin), save it as dated markdown under /workspace/market-intel/briefings/, then create the briefing routine at their chosen time in their timezone. Never invent numbers, quotes, or links, and never post, like, or message anything.

routines.name: Morning chatter briefing
routines.description: Fires each weekday morning to send the owner a briefing on the biggest online conversations in the topics they track.
routines.content:
Put together the owner's morning briefing on what people are talking about, covering roughly the last 24 hours (since the previous briefing; on Monday cover the weekend). Cover the topics the owner asked to track, as saved in memory. Read X through the connected X connector (look up its current tools first, and keep searches targeted to save credits), plus Hacker News, relevant subreddits via Reddit's public JSON, and the news. Read only: never post, like, follow, bookmark, or message anyone.

For each topic, pick the 3 to 5 biggest conversations, each with one plain-English sentence on what happened and why people care, a rough size signal taken from what you actually fetched (engagement, points, upvotes), and its real source link. Add a short note on anything showing up across several places at once. Never invent numbers, quotes, or links, and skip items already covered in recent briefings unless they meaningfully moved. Save the full briefing as markdown under /workspace/market-intel/briefings/ named by date.

Send the briefing to the owner in this chat, kept skimmable. If a source fails, still send what you have and say which source was thin.

Fires on:
- cron `CRON_TZ=Asia/Calcutta 57 7 * * 1-5`

Ask the importing user for:
- Timezone
